Amihere played her first two seasons, 2023 and '24, with the Dream. The 25-year-old had intel to relay. "Just tendencies," Amihere said. item.description: Texas State outfielder Jackson Cotton (44) swings at a pitch during the game against Louisiana at Bobcat Ballpark on Saturday, March. 21, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Texas State baseball unveiled its 2027 schedule as it prepares for its first season in the Pac-12. The Bobcats begin their season Feb. 21 with a three-game series against Oakland. They will face Texas , Texas A&M and Baylor in a trio of home-and-home series. They'll visit Oklahoma State before the Round Rock Tournament in February and host Houston in May. MORE: How Bobcats stack up in new Pac-12 Of Texas State's 56 regular-season games, it'll host 33 at home in Irvine-Rasmussen Ballpark, according to a news release last week. The baseball team's first Pac-12 weekend series begins April 9 against Gonzaga. Texas State hosts UTSA on March 30 in the I-35 Rivalry and travels to San Antonio on April 13 to complete the series. Oregon State, Washington State, Fresno State, San Diego State, Gonzaga and Dallas Baptist are Texas State's rivals in Pac-12 play. Texas State went 37-26 in 2026 and hit a program-record 116 home runs , earning a berth to the NCAA tournament College Station regionals . It upset USC in a dramatic opening game before its elimination from the bracket. The Bobcats retained key contributors in the offseason such as catcher Clayton Namken, outfielder Jaquae Stewart, utility Ethan Farris, infielder Tanner Carson, outfielder Jackson Cotton and left-handed pitcher Jesus Tovar. item.title: UConn and Michigan State meet again, with Braylon Mullins’ status still unclear
item.description: UConn and Michigan State meet again, with Braylon Mullins’ status still unclear originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . UConn and Michigan State meet Tuesday in East Lansing for an exhibition that has more history than a typical preseason tune-up. The Huskies beat the Spartans 76-69 in last season’s exhibition, then won 67-63 in the Sweet 16 in March. Now they face each other again with UConn ranked No. 4 and Michigan State No. 6 in the preseason AP poll. There is also a meaningful question about the Huskies’ lineup. Braylon Mullins missed UConn’s exhibition opener against Syracuse with an undisclosed injury, and his status for Tuesday had not been confirmed as of Monday. Coach Dan Hurley had not disclosed whether Mullins would be available. A familiar opponent, but not a regular-season game The exhibition gives both teams an early look at how their rosters handle a high-level opponent. Michigan State returns five of its top eight scorers from last season and is led by guard Jeremy Fears Jr. UConn’s opening exhibition against Syracuse offered an early look at its new group, but Mullins was absent. BREAKING: Michigan State is ranked No. 6 to start the season. They will host No. 4 UConn tomorrow in an exhibition game. https://t.co/x8pp3X6uLu — Michigan State Content (@msucontent) October 19, 2026 The setting matters, too. The game is at Michigan State’s Breslin Center, where the Spartans will get a home-court atmosphere even though the result will not count in the regular-season standings. It tips at 7 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday. MORE : Kentucky is two AP poll appearances from a milestone no other program has reached Mullins’ availability is the detail to watch Mullins’ absence does not automatically change the meaning of the exhibition, and there is no confirmed diagnosis or timetable in the available update. But a game against a ranked opponent is a useful chance to test lineups before the regular season. If he is unavailable again, UConn will have to evaluate its options without one of its key guards. The recent history gives this matchup some extra spice, but the early-season value is practical: how do these teams look, and who is ready to play? The scoreboard will not settle anything in October. The lineup decisions could still tell us something. item.title: Highlights! Former UFC fighter Jimmie Rivera delivers filthy knockout in BKFC 95 co-main
item.description: “El Terror” made sure his hometown crowd had something to celebrate. Former Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) fighter Jimmie Rivera returned to the Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC) ring this past weekend (Sat., Oct. 17, 2026) at BKFC 95, where he faced Brandon Meyer in the co-main event inside the Prudential Center in Newark, N.J. Rivera, a New Jersey native, delivered one of the night’s most memorable finishes with a brutal fourth-round knockout. Rivera pressed forward and backed Meyer toward the ropes, steadily closing the distance as Meyer tried to hold his ground. Once Meyer was trapped along the perimeter, Rivera found his opening and fired a clean left hook upstairs. The punch landed flush, sending Meyer face-first to the canvas. The referee quickly stepped in to stop the fight at 46 seconds of the fourth round. Rivera has built a new chapter of his combat sports career in bare- knuckle boxing after a lengthy run in mixed martial arts (MMA). A former UFC and Bellator competitor, he last fought in MMA in 2021, when he lost to Pedro Munhoz … in a banger fight. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the New York Giants running back looking for someone to fill in that top spot, one would think the clear answer is Cam Skattebo , though the 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints featured a jam at the position. As Giants running back Najee Harris admitted confusion over the situation, head coach John Harbaugh would respond to his player’s thoughts. Harris would say to the media that “it’s hard to get in a rhythm with one or two plays,” admitting that he has “never been through none of this before,” according to Greg Johnson. “Harbaugh would be asked about Harris ‘ comments, saying that the rushing attack “hasn’t earned” a “circumstance” to that of Baltimore Ravens’ Derrick Henry or Philadelphia Eagles’ Saquon Barkley. “I do understand it, respect it. Also understand that that’s earned. I would love for us to be in that kind of a circumstance, a Derrick Henry circumstance or the Saquon Barkley circumstance … that would be great,” Harbaugh said, per Greg Johnson. “Our run game hasn’t earned that yet. None of those guys have. My advice would be to any player…’Do the most you can with the opportunities you get. Make the most of those opportunities, and you’re sure to get more opportunities. McCarthy with 26 yards, but the leading running back was Tyrone Tracy Jr. at six carries for 18 yards. item.title: Kentucky is two AP poll appearances from a milestone no other program has reached
item.description: Kentucky is two AP poll appearances from a milestone no other program has reached originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kentucky opens the 2026-27 men’s basketball season at No. 23 in the AP Top 25. The ranking carries an unusual bit of history: the Wildcats have now appeared in the weekly AP poll 998 times, more than any other program. If they remain ranked for the next two polls, they will become the first team to reach 1,000 appearances. That is a measure of consistency across generations, not a prediction for this season. A poll appearance means Kentucky was ranked in a particular weekly edition; it does not mean the Wildcats won a game or a championship. But staying in the national conversation that many times requires a program to keep producing teams voters believe belong among the country’s best. No. 23 puts the milestone within reach Kentucky’s current ranking is enough to keep the count moving. The AP report noted the 998th appearance and said two more weeks would put the Wildcats at 1,000. The careful distinction is that Kentucky needs to remain in the poll for those appearances to count. The first edition of the AP Poll for college basketball came out today, and Kentucky came in at No. 23! Is this too high or too low for Mark Pope’s Wildcats? https://t.co/krTscNmSUo — Chatterbox Sports (@CBoxSports) October 20, 2026 The Wildcats also enter a season with a demanding schedule. Kentucky’s athletics department lists nine opponents ranked ahead of it in the preseason AP and coaches polls, including Florida, Texas, Tennessee, Virginia and Louisville. That gives the team plenty of chances to make a statement, but also plenty of opportunities to test its place in the rankings. It is built by staying relevant over decades, through different coaches, rosters and eras of college basketball. Kentucky’s No. 23 start puts the Wildcats close to a round number that no other program has reached. The immediate goal is simple: keep winning enough to stay ranked. The historical one is close enough for fans to track every Monday. If Kentucky holds its place, a routine poll release could become a milestone moment. Coach Sean McVay ’s Los Angeles Rams are 2-4 and in danger of falling out of playoff contention heading into Week 7 after injures have ravaged them, including one to Davante Adams . item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Pittsburgh Steelers are reportedly searching for help at wide receiver, and two players familiar to coach Mike McCarthy offer an intriguing connection. With injuries thinning Pittsburgh’s receiving corps, NFL Network insider Tom Pelissero reports that the Steelers have been contacting teams about potential additions. That creates the possibility of McCarthy turning to players he previously coached with the Dallas Cowboys. The reported search is real. Whether it produces a Dallas reunion remains an open question. Steelers Are Calling About Veteran Receivers According to Behind the Steel Curtain’s account of Pelissero’s reporting , Pittsburgh began exploring the market after injuries hit the position. “I do know the Steelers have been calling around on veteran receivers since the injuries last week,” Pelissero wrote in his subscriber chat at The Sweep , as quoted by the outlet. Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson are on injured reserve. Ben Skowronek also missed the Week 6 matchup with Tampa Bay because of a leg injury, further reducing Pittsburgh’s options. Those absences create a practical problem. Pittsburgh needs enough dependable receivers to operate its offense while avoiding excessive demands on the players who remain available. A veteran addition could provide immediate insurance without requiring the Steelers to pursue a blockbuster. item.title: Mel Kiper Jr. thinks Arch Manning has ‘got to go back to college for another year’
item.description: Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The draft guru has spoken. The Texas Longhorns entered the 2026 college football season as a trendy pick for national champion, and they seemed to be living up to that promise after beating Ohio State and becoming the No. 1 team in the nation. However, after consecutive losses to unranked teams (Oklahoma, Florida), the Longhorns are free-falling, and much of the blame is being foisted on quarterback Arch Manning . Manning, the nephew of Peyton and Eli, came into the season with Heisman hype, but has disappointed with his inconsistency and lack of growth. It’s gotten to the point where the guy once considered a presumed No. 1 pick in the NFL Draft is being told to stay in school another year. And it’s not just anyone telling him that. Longtime ESPN draft analyst Mel Kiper Jr. is the one saying it. “All I’ll say is right now, you’ve got to go back to college for another year,” Kiper said Monday on First Draft . “And if you don’t, it’s got to be the Green Bay Packer model of Jordan Love and Aaron Rodgers where you’ve got your guy and you’re picking late first round, and you’ve got your quarterback for another three years – I’m saying three years. I’m not saying one, I’m not saying two. “Patrick Mahomes sat for a year. Let’s forget the year. For Arch, I think it’s three years. It’s got to be the Jordan Love, Aaron Rodgers, Green Bay Packers model if he comes out.” It’s not as though Manning hasn’t put up big numbers. He’s completed 63.9% of his passes for 1,295 yards, 11 touchdowns, and five interceptions this year. Last season, he threw for 3,163 yards and 26 touchdowns, with seven interceptions. However, he’s made some backbreaking mistakes you wouldn’t expect from a highly touted prospect , and that has Kiper thinking he still needs to show something before he’s ready to move up a level. “In every game, you get the good, the bad and the ugly,” Kiper said. “That’s what you’re getting. It’s a wild ride. It’s going to be up, down and around. You might get a quarter, you might get a series, you might get a glimpse, you might get, maybe, a half. But you’re not going to get consistency. You’re just not going to. I keep waiting and waiting and waiting for that game.” The post Mel Kiper Jr. thinks Arch Manning has ‘got to go back to college for another year’ appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.description: Eighty-eight players have received 2026 All-State Soccer honors from the South Dakota High School Soccer Coaches Association. Rolfing made the second team and Sonnichsen the first team in 2025. State Runner-up Watertown — Roger Carranza, Xane Fligge and Owen Muller (first team), Matthew Bertsch (second team) and Isaac Thorson (honorable mention). Fligge made the second team in 2025. Other First Team — Linus Johnson, Aberdeen Central; Oakley McMillen, Sioux Falls Jefferson; Miles Wright, Rapid City Stevens; Carson Johnson, Sioux Falls Washington and Evan Duncan, Spearfish. McMillen is a repeat first-team selection. Wright moved up after making the second team last fall. Other Second Team — Gus Bjerknes, Aberdeen Central; Liam Weide, Harrisburg; Caiden Ahartz and Jacob LaRoche, Pierre; Ravi Moreland, Rapid City Stevens; Trey Woods, Sioux Falls Jefferson; Carson Coulter, Sioux Falls Washington; and Antonio Guitron, Yankton. item.title: Ravens’ Jesse Minter Provides Critical Update on 2-Pro Bowler After Week 6 Loss to Browns
item.description: Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter. Getty The Baltimore Ravens are coming off a tough 13-10 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, and a few key offensive injuries contributed to the defeat. Baltimore was down quarterback Lamar Jackson for a second game, and it was out center Cam Jurgens. Jurgens suffered a concussion in Week 4 while with the Philadelphia Eagles. The Ravens traded for Jurgens on Oct. 7, sending a 2027 fifth-round and 2028 second-round pick for Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick. The two-time Pro Bowl center has yet to play for the Ravens, but he could appear soon. Head coach Jesse Minter told the media on Monday that Jurgens has come a long way. “Minter said that Cam Jurgens (concussion) has come a long way over the past couple of days and he feels like he has a chance to play Sunday,” Jeff Zrebiec wrote on X. Jurgens Was With the Eagles Since 2022 The Eagles drafted Jurgens with the 51st pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, and he played in 62 games, starting 45. Jurgens made two Pro Bowls in 2024 and 2025, and the Eagles signed him to a four-year, $68 million contract extension in April of 2025. Now Jurgens should play a major role for the Ravens, who let their starting center, Tyler Linderbaum, walk in free agency this past offseason and sign with the Las Vegas Raiders . The Ravens will host the Cincinnati Bengals , and hopefully Jurgens and Jackson will be back for Sunday’s game. item.title: Packers Eyeing Move For Former 1st Round Nose Tackle
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 18: Head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers looks on prior to the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field on October 18, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers have suffered a brutal string of injuries at the heart of the defensive line. Consequently, the team could look to add some faces to the unit that currently only has four players on the active roster. It appears that one name on the Packers’ radar is former Dallas Cowboys first round pick Mazi Smith, whom the team worked out on Monday. The Packers hosted DT Mazi Smith for a tryout, per the wire. He was a Cowboys first-round pick in 2023. Also has played for the Jets and Dolphins. — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) October 19, 2026 “The Packers hosted DT Mazi Smith for a tryout, per the wire. He was a Cowboys first-round pick in 2023. Also has played for the Jets and Dolphins.” The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman posted on X on Monday afternoon. The Packers Have Multiple Injuries at Nose Tackle Starting nose tackle Javon Hargrave is out for the season with an Achilles tear suffered in Week 5’s dominating win against the Chicago Bears in garbage time, whilst backup NT Jonathan Ford was also ruled out of Week 6 with a calf injury. Anthony Campbell, who has deputized at the position twice this season, has also been dealing with an ankle injury, although he was cleared to play this past weekend, where he logged 32 snaps on defense. That leaves only rookie Chris McClellan as a fully healthy option at the position, and even that is tenuous given that the 2026 third round pick’s favored position is at defensive tackle as a 3 technique, rather than as 1 or 0 technique pivot on the defensive line. Mazi Smith Has Struggled Since Entering the NFL So Mazi Smith seems like a reasonable name to add given the circumstances. The 6’3, 337 lb behemoth was once listed as the no. 1 ranked “ freak ” in The Athletic’s Bruce Feldman’s annual piece back in 2022, before being taken with the 26th overall pick in 2023 by Dallas. After two sub-par seasons that saw inconsistent play and a fluctuation in weight by as much as 30-40 lbs, Smith was included as part of the trade that saw Quinnen Williams join the Cowboys from the Jets. The former Michigan man played 5 games with no starts in 2025 and was ultimately released on Aug. 30 during final cuts this year, before being signed to the Miami Dolphins ‘ practice squad, from which he was later released on Oct. 13. Smith reads as a reclamation project for whomever wants to try. For the Packers, in needing depth at nose tackle and getting a potentially freakishly-high upside, there is little to lose in signing the 25-year old to a deal, if his workout went well. item.title: Purdue basketball’s 79-week AP Top 25 streak ends before the season begins
item.description: Purdue basketball’s 79-week AP Top 25 streak ends before the season begins originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Purdue’s streak of 79 consecutive weeks in the AP Top 25 is over. The Boilermakers received 53 points in Monday’s preseason poll, but that was not enough to place them in the top 25. It is a notable change for a program that had been a fixture in the rankings for more than a year and a half. The streak’s end is a snapshot of the poll’s current expectations, not a verdict on what Purdue can accomplish. The preseason vote arrives before a regular-season game has been played. A team can climb quickly once it starts winning, and an unranked team can still become a factor in March. A poll omission still changes the conversation Purdue’s 53 points show that voters did not ignore the Boilermakers. They placed just outside the top 25, among the teams receiving votes. Still, going from a 79-week streak to an unranked preseason position changes the way the season is framed: Purdue will have to earn its way back into the weekly rankings. The AP poll is not a standings table, and it does not award tournament bids. It is a weekly judgment from media voters about the teams they believe are strongest. Purdue’s run ending is therefore a useful marker of shifting expectations, but it should not be confused with a forecast of the team’s final record. MORE : Kansas freshman Tyran Stokes receives major honor as Big 12 poll delivers surprising Jayhawks verdict Houston now owns the active streak While Purdue’s run ends, Houston holds the longest active AP Top 25 streak at 127 weeks and counting, according to the AP. That contrast gives the poll a small bit of historical context: a long ranking streak is difficult to maintain, even for established programs. Here’s a college basketball statistic that caught my attention. Purdue is OUT of the preseason AP Top 25. That ends a streak of 79 consecutive poll appearances for the Boilermakers. Matt Painter has built one of the country’s most consistent programs. Now Purdue has something to prove. — Rodney Knuppel (@KnuppelRodney) October 19, 2026 The Boilermakers can make the streak a footnote by playing well. A strong start would put them back in the conversation quickly. But for now, the poll has handed Purdue an early-season storyline: a program that had been ranked week after week must show voters, and everyone else, why it belongs back in that group. item.title: Cowboys WR George Pickens Called Out for Lack of Effort After Packers Loss
item.description: Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens. Getty The Dallas Cowboys are struggling in epic fashion, and if their offense starts playing like their miserable defense, things could get even worse. Off to a 2-4 start following a lackluster Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers, one high-profile player on that offense finds himself in the crosshairs — NFL All-Pro wide receiver George Pickens. Pickens had 6 receptions for 73 yards in the 23-13 loss to the Packers and has 33 receptions for 428 yards and 1 touchdown on 52 targets through the first six games. When we look at where Pickens was at this point in 2025 — 36 receptions for 525 yards and 6 touchdowns on 51 targets — we start to see the drop-off. That’s just on paper. How Pickens carries himself on the field is under scrutiny again in 2026 — mainly because he’s seemed checked out at times. George Pickens Playing on Franchise Tag in 2026 Pickens is on a 1-year, $27.2 million franchise tag in 2026 after the Cowboys decided against a lucrative contract extension. “I don’t know who was less interested in the (Cowboys-Packers) game tonight other than me, but George Pickens was up there,” The Ringer’s Bill Simmons said on Sunday night . “Pickens thinks the franchise tag means that he’s playing tag football, not actual football. George Pickens Blasted for Lack of Effort in 2025 Pickens was put on blast for a lack of effort in 2025 — almost the same criticism Simmons brought up on Sunday. In a Week 14 loss to the Detroit Lions , Pickens caught 5 passes for 37 yards on 9 targets and picked up two costly penalties: illegal hands to the face and offensive pass interference. His lack of effort in that game brought a stinging rebuke from former NFL cornerback and Super Bowl champion Richard Sherman afterward. “George Pickens seemed uninterested in playing football tonight,” Sherman said on the NFL on Prime postgame broadcast. “He seemed completely disengaged; he disappeared and half-assed it. Totally unacceptable.” “It’s just lackadaisical play and you cannot have an off and on switch,” former NFL wide receiver and ESPN analyst Harry Douglas said on “Get Up” on Friday, December 5. “Every time you take the field you have to say you’re gonna dominate the man across from me. Everything you have to do has to be full speed.” It was the same criticism Pickens got hit with after a Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in 2025. “Not enough effort, not enough commitment to the team,” former NFL offensive lineman and 3-time Pro Bowler Taylor Lewan said on ESPN’s “Get Up” in September 2025. “(The Cowboys ) need more from you when the ball’s not coming your way. There needs to be a full package of commitment from George Pickens … you’re a massively talented young man but we can’t have you jogging in run concepts. You’ve gotta be all in. item.title: Leafs’ Auston Matthews Reveals Where He Stands With Mitch Marner
item.description: Mitch Marner details emotional phone call with Auston Matthews after leaving Maple Leafs. Getty Mitch Marner details emotional phone call with Auston Matthews after leaving Maple Leafs. Getty It’s now been over a year since the Toronto Maple Leafs traded forward Mitch Marner in a blockbuster deal to the Vegas Golden Knights, and both organizations couldn’t have had a more polar opposite 2025-26 season. With the Golden Knights, Marner found himself in the conversation for the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP, helping Vegas reach the Stanley Cup Final before they were eventually defeated by the Carolina Hurricanes. Meanwhile, the Maple Leafs missed the playoffs, and went through an extensive housecleaning under new general manager John Chayka, and entered this current season with a vastly different coaching staff, front office, and a new-look roster. Auston Matthews, who is back and fully healthy after missing several games last season, recent went on record on how his current relationship with Marner is. Auston Matthews Comes Clean On Current Relationship With Former Toronto Maple Leafs Teammate Mitch Marner Getty Mitch Marner details emotional phone call with Auston Matthews after leaving Maple Leafs. Before the Maple Leafs faced Marner and the Golden Knights earlier this month, Matthews revealed that he still keeps in touch with his former teammate and was happy to see his playoff success in Vegas. “Personally as a friend, I was happy for him,” Matthews said of Marner’s run to the Stanley Cup Final earlier in the spring . “We still keep in touch a lot. He’s a great person, great teammate, great friend. It’ll be nice to see him tonight.” So far this season, Marner has scored twice while adding nine assists in 10 games played, once again putting up the points at just over a point-per-game pace. Meanwhile, Matthews looks more like his old self, having already tallied six goals in nine games, a 55-goal pace over a full season. Mitch Marner Revealed “Dark Days” With Maple Leafs Not long after the Stanley Cup Final concluded, Marner revealed that he had been living through some “dark” times while with the Maple Leafs. “There were some really dark moments there, that the thought of playing hockey was just really tough, honestly, in a lot of ways,” Marner said . “Just a dark kind of vibe, a dark hole in a way.” “I think when you’re in that mental blender, it puts a lot of stress on your body, on your mind,” Marner said. “You’re up a lot of nights thinking about how you can be better and change things. You should never be afraid to talk about your emotions and talk about your fears and what you’re going through. “I’m super thankful that I had a lot of people in my life that I could talk to and share things. It made me better.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Leafs’ Auston Matthews Reveals Where He Stands With Mitch Marner appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Former Thunder Championship Player Cut by Kings
item.description: Thunder Adam Flagler Kings Getty Former Oklahoma City Thunder shooting guard Adam Flagler was released by the Sacramento Kings during their final roster cuts. Plenty of teams around the NBA are making their final roster decisions on Monday, and it cost the former Thunder player Flagler his job. Kings Release Adam Flagler With NBA teams making their final roster decisions ahead of Monday’s roster deadline, the Kings decided to release Flagler from his two-way contract with the team, which means he immediately becomes a free agent. “Kings waive two-way player Adam Flagler,” wrote Kings reporter James Ham on X. Kings waive two-way player Adam Flagler: pic.twitter.com/JsaAWkBgTu — James Ham (@James_HamNBA) October 19, 2026 Adam Flagler Won NBA Championship With Thunder Flagler has played two seasons in the NBA, both for the Thunder. In 2023-24, Flagler had a cup of coffee in the NBA, playing in just two games with the Thunder. But in 2024-25, Flagler had a much larger audition with Oklahoma City, as he played in 37 games with the team. The Thunder won the NBA Championship in 2025, and Flagler received a ring despite not getting a chance to play during the playoffs. Last year, Flagler signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the San Antonio Spurs and played the entire season in the G League with the Austin Spurs, as he did not get a call-up back to the NBA. He was hoping to get a chance to play in the NBA again this season with Sacramento, but clearly, that will not happen, as the team decided to let him go. Could he return to Oklahoma City? It’s possible, since he had a successful run with the team during their championship-winning season two years ago, although he would likely have to sign another Exhibit 10 deal to play in the G League. We’ll see where Flagler ends up, as there could be another NBA team that shows interest in him as a potential two-way player. But regardless of where he ultimately ends up in the NBA, the G League, or in Europe, Flagler can always hold his head up high as he is an NBA champion, and not everyone who plays in the league can say that they won an NBA championship ring. item.title: Red Wings Ready To Flip The Script In Kraken Rematch On Tuesday
item.description: Follow Michael Whitaker On X After playing seven of their first eight home games of the 2026-27 NHL campaign, the Detroit Red Wings have hit the road for their next four outings. They'll start their road trip with a rematch against the Seattle Kraken on Monday evening, and will hope to exact some revenge for their 6-3 defeat at Little Caesars Arena earlier in the month. The Red Wings vastly outplayed the Kraken in the first period of their contest, enjoying a decided shots advantage. After an early second-period goal from William Wallinder, things fell apart for Detroit, who allowed three goals in a span of 3:05. “I thought we played - that was the game we played a really solid 45 minutes, but a horrible 15 minutes in the middle of the game,” said forward Andrew Copp. “I think we just have to stick with that plan. I thought we had a really good first (period)...we just have to find that blend where we're moving our feet and checking well, and playing direct. “It’s not a real secret recipe, it’s just, can we do it night in and night out?” Bookmark The Hockey News Detroit Red Wings team site to stay connected to the latest news , game-day coverage, and player features . Red Wings head coach Todd McLellan was adamant about the team's need to win “scrappy” hockey games following their 4-3 shootout victory over the San Jose Sharks on Saturday evening, a message that first-year Red Wings forward Viktor Arvidsson echoed. "I think we're good when we have volume shooting and being good on the forecheck, keeping pucks alive after the initial shot," he said. "I think we can do a little bit better job of getting those second opportunities in front of the net and bury those kind of chances." "He's Playing Catch-Up": Head Coach Todd McLellan Speaks On Dylan Larkin's First Six Games Detroit Red Wings head coach Todd McLellan offered his take on Dylan Larkin's performance since returning from an upper-body injury earlier this month. Arvidsson also referenced the unwanted result against the Kraken earlier in the month, noting that it was the one game that's gotten away from them this season in what has otherwise been a heavily competitive output for the club. "I think we've been in every game, we've been close in every game - I think that Seattle game got away from us," he said. "We just have to keep trying." item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Bruised Bundesliga champions hit a supposed rival for six and their flying winger is peaking at a perfect moment When Bayern Munich fail to win for two games in a row, you know what is coming next. Particularly on a Saturday night showcase, against the sort of good domestic opposition that tend to bring the best out of the champions. It had been a frustrating week, domestically and continentally, in two games on the road. On both occasions they had been caught cold, conceding the Bundesliga’s fastest goal at Augsburg and going 1-0 down in less than 90 seconds in Stavanger . Vincent Kompany’s low profile on the Allianz Arena touchline, almost motionless in his seat as his team rattled a flurry of goals past poor RB Leipzig, had nothing to do with any lingering chagrin connected to those slow starts from his team. The sporting director, Max Eberl, who stood in for his coach in the post-match press conference, explained that the Belgian had been ill, not to mention Kompany’s current hip problem that had made the move from dressing room to pitchside slow and uncomfortable. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Last year, he was involved in US friendlies against Ecuador and Australia. But this year, with Fifa having folded the October window into September, Pulisic didn’t have the chance. On Sunday, his pre-match music was O Generosa, the Serie A anthem, which he observed with a soft smile. Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years with Milan. The magnificence: 43 goals and 25 assists in 138 appearances. The misery: just one trophy since he arrived in July 2023, a 2025 Supercoppa Italia held in Saudi Arabia. Continue reading...

item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
